title: The reasoning door drops total_cost_usd from an is_error envelope, so a failed seat turn books nothing
body:
## Summary
lib/claudeCli.ts::settleEnvelope throws a bare CliError for is_error/non-success and discards the envelope's total_cost_usd.

## Description
The retrieval rung now carries a failed run's cost (793de075, RetrieveRunFailed). The reasoning door (lib/claudeCli.ts:318-331) does not: `if (j.is_error || j.subtype !== "success") throw new CliError(...)` loses `j.total_cost_usd`, so a reason() turn that ran and ended error_during_execution leaves no text-usd row (spend.ts books only a vendor-reported cost on the error's detail). Fix: the same subclass shape (a CliError carrying costUsd) and providers/claudeCli.ts passing it to cliTextError's `detail` (the seam 4def8262 added). lib/claudeCli.ts is outside this context (it is the shared transport, also used by pipeline/direct-frames.mts).

## Flow
- fake engine plays `# DOOR is_error` (total_cost_usd 0.0004)
- reason() rejects failed; bookFailedTurn sees no detail.costUsd
- the 0.0004 is booked as unpriced (dispatched) since c8c1e4d2, not as its figure

## Expected impact
The ledger carries the seat's reported figure for errored runs. Could break: a caller that matches CliError by exact class (none found: grep instanceof CliError).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed reasoning turn books its reported cost
Before: # DOOR is_error -> 0 $ rows (cost 0.0004 reported)
After: 1 failed row 0.0004 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked the cassette through settleEnvelope; the file is out of this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: lib/claudeCli.ts:325-326; tests/_engine/cassettes/engine-door.json turn '# DOOR is_error' total_cost_usd 0.0004
instrument: tests/golden-path/text-spend.probe.spec.ts case: withFakeEngine(engine-door) reason('# DOOR is_error') -> expect 1 failed row amount 0.0004

title: .ai/use-cases.json declares no use case for research, ad-ideas or ad-scenarios
body:
## Summary
lighttrack.ts emits `text.<turn>` for every TurnClass; .ai/use-cases.json declares 12 of the 15, missing text.research, text.ad-ideas and text.ad-scenarios.

## Description
lib/text/lighttrack.ts:85 names every event `text.${l.turn}`, and its header says the use-case file is what those names hang off. .ai/use-cases.json lists text.edit-plan, compose, scene-direction, style-synthesis, sound-hunt, sound-lesson, suno-propose, suno-riff, mv-treatment, mv-metadata, repair, probe (plus article-* and strip-author, not TurnClass members) - so the app's dearest turn (research) and both ad rounds report against undeclared names, which the file's own note calls the coverage gap. The file is outside this context; registering it in LightTrack (`lt use-cases register`) is an operator act.

## Flow
- walk TurnClass (lib/text/types.ts union)
- diff against use_cases[].key with the text. prefix
- 3 missing

## Expected impact
LightTrack's coverage report stops showing research/ad events as undeclared. Could break: nothing in-tree reads the file at runtime.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every emitted name is declared
Before: 12 of 15 TurnClass keys declared
After: 15 of 15
Method: probe - node over .ai/use-cases.json against the union
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: node -e use_cases keys -> no text.research / text.ad-ideas / text.ad-scenarios; lib/text/types.ts:212-227
instrument: a probe asserting every TurnClass member has a `text.<turn>` key in .ai/use-cases.json (walk the union as text-ladder.probe now does)

title: The trail records an invalid-request (and unsupported/no-alternative) as `failed`
body:
## Summary
router.ts::trailReason maps every kind outside RerouteStep's vocabulary to `failed`, so the size-cap refusal logs `tried=google:failed` beside `kind=invalid-request`.

## Description
RerouteStep['why'] (lib/text/types.ts:279-297) has no `invalid-request`; trailReason (lib/text/router.ts, switch) returns `failed` for it. Measured this round in the size-cap case's log line: `kind=invalid-request ... tried=google:failed`. The router header's promise is that descent reasons are in the trail's own vocabulary so a fleet's descent is diagnosable; `failed` here reads as an engine fault when nothing was sent. RerouteStep is consumed outside lib/text (packages/kernel router trail copies `why`), so widening the union needs those consumers enumerated.

## Flow
- reason() with a prompt past the cap
- adapter throws invalid-request
- trail entry why=failed

## Expected impact
A descent record that says what happened. Could break: a consumer switching exhaustively on RerouteStep.why.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - trail vocabulary matches the error kind
Before: invalid-request -> trail 'failed' (1 reproduced line)
After: trail 'invalid-request'
Method: probe - the text-ladder size-cap case's log line
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: [text] edit-plan err kind=invalid-request provider=google ... tried=google:failed (sw-tre-a5.log); lib/text/router.ts trailReason default branch
instrument: text-ladder size-cap case extended: expect the refusal's trail (detail or log) to carry 'invalid-request'; grep consumers of RerouteStep.why

title: retrieve() with `avoid` emptying its chain says nothing may retrieve, where reason() says no-alternative
body:
## Summary
router.ts::retrieve filters `avoid` and, when that empties the chain, refuses 'Nothing may retrieve for a research turn in local posture' (kind unsupported) - false: a candidate was planned and the caller avoided it.

## Description
reason() goes through orderFor, which throws noAlternative when avoid empties the plan (lib/text/router.ts orderFor). retrieve() filters inline (walk: `retrievePlanFor(...).filter((id) => id !== req.avoid)`) and falls through to the bottom with `first` null, so the message names no candidate and the kind is `unsupported`. The mirror is not a one-line fix: lib/turns/kinds/research.ts:133 falls back to reason() only when the retrieval error is reroutable or `unsupported`, so a `no-alternative` there would turn today's fallback into a failed research run. Needs the caller's rule decided with it.

## Flow
- retrieve({turn:'research', avoid:'claude-cli-retrieve'}) with TEXT_RETRIEVE=1
- message: 'Tried: no candidates were planned. Nothing may retrieve ...'

## Expected impact
An honest refusal sentence. Could break: research's fallback-to-reason, if the kind changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the refusal names the avoided candidate
Before: message claims nothing was planned (walked)
After: names the avoided candidate, kind kept fallback-compatible
Method: simulation - walked retrieve() and research.ts:133; not built because the kind is a contract with the research kind
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: lib/text/router.ts retrieve walk first line; lib/turns/kinds/research.ts:133
instrument: research-retrieve.probe case: retrieve with avoid -> message names claude-cli-retrieve and research still falls back to reason

title: engineStatus spawns `claude --version` twice when retrieval is on
body:
## Summary
engineStatus probes every unblocked candidate, and with TEXT_RETRIEVE=1 the research row lists claude-cli-retrieve and claude-cli - the same binary, whose probe() is claudeCliProvider().probe().

## Description
lib/text/router.ts engineStatus loops `[...retrievePlanFor(turn), ...planFor(turn)]` and awaits `PROVIDERS[id]().probe()` per id; providers/claudeCliRetrieve.ts probe() delegates to claudeCliProvider().probe(), which spawns `claude --version` (lib/claudeCli.ts probeClaude). Two sequential spawns on Windows (cmd.exe shim) for one answer. A per-call memo keyed on the probe function would make it one.

## Flow
- TEXT_RETRIEVE=1; GET the research pre-flight
- two `--version` spawns, sequential

## Expected impact
Halves the pre-flight's spawn cost. Could break: nothing, the answers are identical by construction.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - spawns per pre-flight
Before: 2 spawns (walked)
After: 1
Method: simulation - read the delegation; a fake engine's --version log would count it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/text/router.ts engineStatus loop; lib/text/providers/claudeCliRetrieve.ts probe(): return claudeCliProvider().probe()
instrument: withFakeEngine + FAKE_CLAUDE_LOG: count --version invocations for engineStatus('research') with TEXT_RETRIEVE=1

title: Google's model and base URL overrides are captured at module load, unlike every key
body:
## Summary
providers/google.ts reads GOOGLE_TEXT_BASE_URL, GOOGLE_TEXT_MODEL and GOOGLE_TEXT_MODEL_PLAN once at import (BASE, MODEL_FOR_TURN), while env.ts's header makes lazy per-call reads the rule.

## Description
lib/text/env.ts header: 'Keys are read lazily, per call ... a route handler that booted before .env.local was filled in would otherwise hold a stale absence'. lib/text/providers/google.ts:46 and :113-151 evaluate process.env at module load, so a model override set after boot is ignored until restart, and a test that sets GOOGLE_TEXT_MODEL after import cannot steer the adapter. Fix: resolve per call (a function over the table).

## Flow
- import router (google.ts loads)
- set GOOGLE_TEXT_MODEL=gemini-x
- a turn still names the default model

## Expected impact
Overrides behave like keys. Could break: nothing; the defaults are unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - config read when used
Before: 3 env reads at load (walked)
After: 0 at load
Method: simulation - read the module; a probe setting the var after import would decide it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/text/providers/google.ts:46 const BASE = process.env...; :113 const MODEL_FOR_TURN = {... process.env.GOOGLE_TEXT_MODEL ...}
instrument: text-ladder case: stub fetch, set GOOGLE_TEXT_MODEL after import, assert the URL names it

title: An estimated (priced) Gemini turn books no spend row: the ledger counts only the seat
body:
## Summary
spend.ts books only `vendor-reported` costs; Google's adapter prices with priceTurn (basis `estimated`), so the only real-money engine never writes a $ row, even on a priced model.

## Description
lib/text/spend.ts bookServedTurn: `const vendor = p.costBasis === "vendor-reported" && finite(p.costUsd)` - an estimated cost becomes `unpriced` and bumps a counter. providers/google.ts passes `quote.basis` (estimated whenever a row has rates, today gemini-3.8-flash; every in-service row is unpriced). The operator's memory says only Gemini is real cost, and the claude seat's total_cost_usd is notional - so the ledger books the notional figure and refuses the real one. cost-metering 'estimate before, measure after, track the gap' says the estimate is a row with its basis, not nothing. Booking estimates (basis 'estimate') changes what the text-usd window totals mean - an operator decision on a count-only class (2026-10-07 'Count only, refuse nothing').

## Flow
- a priced Google turn serves with costBasis estimated
- bookServedTurn books unpriced
- text-usd spent excludes it

## Expected impact
Gemini spend becomes visible in the window. Could break: any reader that treats text-usd spent as vendor-reported only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the real-money engine appears in its ledger
Before: 0 $ rows for an estimated Google turn
After: 1 row basis estimate
Method: probe - text-spend card case 4 already shows an unpriced google turn booking 0 rows
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: lib/text/spend.ts bookServedTurn vendor test; lib/text/providers/google.ts quote.basis; lib/text/pricing.ts priceTurn basis 'estimated'

title: gemini-3.8-flash's introductory rate has no machine expiry; it prices at half after 2027-01-01
body:
## Summary
pricing.ts states in prose that the 3.8 row's 0.75/3.75 rate doubles on 2027-01-01, and nothing in priceTurn reads a date.

## Description
lib/text/pricing.ts gemini-3.8-flash row: 'IT IS INTRODUCTORY AND DATED ... DOUBLES to 1.50/7.50 on 2027-01-01 ... this row is wrong from that date'. priceTurn has no clock. The imaging sibling got an ISO-dated quote rule this run (spend-and-pricing: 'A quote day that is not an ISO date cannot keep an ended introductory rate pricing'). The row is not in service today, so the defect is latent until promotion; an `until` field that turns the row unpriced past its date would make the prose a rule.

## Flow
- promote 3.8 into MODEL_FOR_TURN
- 2027-01-02: priceTurn estimates at the introductory rate
- estimate half the bill

## Expected impact
No under-estimate after the rate change. Could break: nothing in service today.

## Evaluation
Claim: risk - a dated price cannot outlive its date
Before: 0 date checks in priceTurn
After: row unpriced past `until`
Method: simulation - walked priceTurn with a 2027 clock
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: packages/kernel/test/pricing.test.ts (or a text pricing probe) case: priceTurn on 3.8 with now=2027-01-02 -> unpriced
